response.markdown_report:
Select **causal gating of convolutional lag contributions** as a controlled NextItNet experiment. At 20% progress, test this modest intervention before adding text encoders or combining objectives; existing evidence does not establish superiority over depth correction or multi-negative training.

Three experimental insights matter. Residual-depth correction scored 0.5325 versus baseline 0.5300, without paired uncertainty. User feedback identifies stale-interest emphasis and broad associations displacing specific recent matches. Sampled training misranking remains 8.22% in Industrial_and_Scientific and 6.67% in Electronics; these observations identify errors without establishing their causes.

Three literature insights refine the proposal. NextItNet provides causal dilated coverage [1], while DynamicConv demonstrates input-dependent temporal kernels [2]. Neither establishes Amazon gains. Sampled-softmax analysis motivates an independent objective comparison [3]. Sampled-ranking research warns that fixed candidate comparisons do not establish full-catalog ranking [4].

The framework separates three directions: **where history enters**, using lag gates; **which existing depth contributes**, using residual-depth correction; and **which items compete during training**, using multi-negative softmax. Test interventions separately.

Scores use O=originality, P=potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment, D=difficulty; higher D means harder. Each cell includes a benefit and limitation.

| Atomic idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Causal lag gates [1,2] | 3: precise adaptation; established dynamic filtering | 6: temporal control; overlapping paths | 7: recent specificity; intent unobserved | 5: changes erroneous features; cause unproven | 6: local adapter; integration and timing |
| Residual-depth correction, supplied inspiration | 3: precise adaptation; established aggregation | 6: inexpensive; redundant depths | 7: context emphasis; stale direct path | 6: adjustable features; weak attribution | 4: small layer; predictor synchronization |
| Moderate uniform multi-negative softmax [3] | 2: established; little novelty | 7: stronger competition; false negatives | 5: specificity pressure; no temporal mechanism | 8: trains ordering; generalization uncertain | 4: unchanged inference; sampling cost |

For the selected idea, multiply historical convolution taps by jointly trained `2*sigmoid(aᵀcurrent+bᵀpast+c)` gates, initialized to one; retain the current-position tap. This targets stale-interest emphasis and broad recommendations displacing recent matches, and tests whether sampled misranking improves. However, within a fixed tap, additive logits cannot reverse the ordering of two past vectors when current context changes. Different taps have different parameters. This is adaptive modulation, with limited explicit compatibility matching; a product-term gate is a later hypothesis.

Retrain all-one, static `2*sigmoid(c)`, and adaptive controls under identical settings. Mean-gate replacement is a separate inference probe. Preserve the objective, one checkpoint/head per category, and fixed protocol. Verify outputs and gradients, causality, padding, save/load consistency and representative runtime before fitting. Prespecify configuration order and checkpoint selection within the shared budget.

Measure complete-output prefix sensitivity and sampled misranking; neither establishes user benefit. Select solely by pinned four-category validation HR@10. Report paired uncertainty only when host outcomes permit; selected-winner bootstraps do not remove adaptive-selection optimism [5,6]. Compatibility, quantity, duplication and purchase intent remain unresolved. No new experiment has been executed.

idea.description: Add identity-initialized, positionwise causal gates to historical tap contributions inside the corrected NextItNet convolutions. Gates are jointly trained with the existing backbone and scoring head. Keep each current-position tap unchanged and deploy exactly one model per category. Compare against retrained all-one and input-independent static-tap controls; never combine their predictions.
idea.motivation: The proposal explicitly targets two observed user failures: older seasonal or secondary interests receiving excessive emphasis, and broadly associated items displacing specific matches to recent activity. It also targets the observed sampled training misranking rates, particularly 8.22% in Industrial_and_Scientific and 6.67% in Electronics. These links remain hypotheses: omitted temporal-sensitivity results do not establish excessive old-history dependence, and training misranking does not establish held-out ranking quality. Unlike aggregating completed residual states, tap gating changes historical contributions before each convolution mixes them. Residual paths still transmit older information, so complete-output effects must be measured. The supplied depth-correction result of 0.5325 versus 0.5300 is a descriptive macro difference of 0.0025, equivalent to two net hits across the four equally sized validation categories if calculated exactly from this protocol; it does not establish significance or justify abandoning depth correction. At this early research stage, lag gating is a controlled alternative, while moderate multi-negative training remains the next independent objective hypothesis. The proposed additive gate can modulate contributions but cannot directly express general current–past compatibility; claims about recognizing specific practical or content needs would exceed the available evidence.
idea.implementation_notes:
The corrected baseline source is not included in the prompt. The code is an integration component, not a fabricated replacement train.py. Replace each existing temporal Conv1d at construction time with CausalTapGateConv, preserving its original weight and bias Parameter objects and dilation. In the block forward, replace the existing explicit-left-padding-plus-convolution operation with adapter(h_BLC, sequence), transposing the existing BCL representation where necessary. The adapter receives unpadded B x L x D states; do not retain the old explicit padding around this call. Preserve the block's original normalization, activation, dropout and residual ordering and mask its intermediate/output states as in the corrected baseline. The adapter supports stride-one, ungrouped causal convolutions with original internal padding zero and rejects unsupported configurations.

For PyTorch cross-correlation, tap k receives lag (K-1-k)*d: tap zero is oldest and tap K-1 is current. Each historical adaptive gate is 2*sigmoid(a_k^T current + b_k^T historical + c_k), initialized to one. Current and historical states are normalized only across channels for the gate; convolution operates on original masked states. Gates lie in (0,2), permitting attenuation or amplification, without guaranteeing recency preference. The current-position contribution and convolution bias are unchanged; add bias exactly once. Zero initialization introduces no extra random draws. Preserve differentiable tensor slices and original Parameters without detach or tensor reconstruction.

The additive logit has a specific expressivity limitation: for a fixed layer and tap and two fixed past vectors, changing the current vector cannot reverse their gate ordering. Cross-tap ordering can still depend on current context because tap parameters differ. Sigmoid coupling, multiplication by historical features, and subsequent nonlinear layers create interactions in the complete network, so it would be inaccurate to call the network interaction-free. One scalar scales all channels equally. A later separately tested variant could add w_k^T(current*historical), permitting context-dependent ordering, but do not add it to the initial experiment or claim that additive gates model exact compatibility. DynamicConv is a more direct architectural reference than GAT4Rec; retain GAT4Rec as adjacent evidence only.

All-one mode retains the original Conv1d computation with explicit left padding and output masking. Static mode learns one c_k per historical tap, and adaptive mode learns a_k, b_k and c_k. Retrain each eligible control from scratch under the same initialization and sampling conventions. Static versus adaptive tests input dependence within this parameterization, but does not control parameter count or optimization flexibility. All-one versus adaptive also changes parameterization and numerical execution. Replacing fitted adaptive gates by their mean or by one is an inexpensive same-network inference intervention, not a retrained static control. Gate-off scores and gradients should agree with the original masked convolution within declared numerical tolerances; equivalent mathematical sums can differ across GPU kernels. Check input, weight and bias gradients, not only outputs, using random upstream gradients and examples spanning short histories, dilations, padding and nonzero biases.

The provided loop avoids materializing every tap simultaneously but launches K projections. A vectorized alternative constructs causal windows using unfold and contracts B x L x K x Cin gated features against the same weights; it may materialize large intermediates. Do not assume either version is faster. Benchmark representative complete forward/backward batches and peak memory before committing to full fitting. Keep the initial implementation fixed after this timing decision, record it in the trial manifest, and include timing/check costs in the shared budget. All dilated convolutions and residual paths still execute; no compute savings are claimed.

Keep the baseline loss, optimizer, sampler, widths, dilation schedule, dropout, weight decay, final transformation and checkpoint schedule unchanged. Do not simultaneously add depth correction, prefix conditioning, text features or multi-negative loss. Record the actual inherited settings rather than inventing their unspecified values. Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per executed epoch. Preserve the host SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200 and cap it at 200. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl; DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; keep artifacts beneath the trial directory and execution on one GPU. Training, failed attempts, integration checks and diagnostics consume the method's shared 43,200 GPU-second allowance; its remaining balance and feasibility are not supplied.

Prefer all-one, static, then adaptive for a controlled comparison if complete four-category configurations fit. If timing and remaining budget cannot support all three, drop the static control before inspecting comparison outcomes and limit attribution claims. idea.pseudocode:
import torch
from torch import nn
import torch.nn.functional as F


class CausalTapGateConv(nn.Module):
    """Replace explicit left padding + stride-one, ungrouped Conv1d.

    Input: unpadded h [B,L,Cin], sequence [B,L], padding ID zero.
    Output: [B,L,Cout]. Keep original block ordering and masking.
    """
    def __init__(self, conv, mode='adaptive', eps=1e-5):
        super().__init__()
        if not isinstance(conv, nn.Conv1d):
            raise TypeError('Expected nn.Conv1d')
        if conv.stride != (1,) or conv.groups != 1:
            raise ValueError('Requires stride-one, ungrouped convolution')
        if conv.padding != (0,) or conv.padding_mode != 'zeros':
            raise ValueError('Requires original explicit causal padding')
        if mode not in ('ones', 'static', 'adaptive') or eps <= 0:
            raise ValueError('Invalid gate configuration')
        self.conv = conv  # Preserve original weight/bias Parameter objects.
        self.mode = mode
        self.eps = float(eps)
        self.kernel_size = conv.kernel_size[0]
        self.dilation = conv.dilation[0]
        historical_taps = self.kernel_size - 1
        if mode == 'adaptive':
            shape = (historical_taps, conv.in_channels)
            self.current_gate = nn.Parameter(conv.weight.new_zeros(shape))
            self.history_gate = nn.Parameter(conv.weight.new_zeros(shape))
        else:
            self.register_parameter('current_gate', None)
            self.register_parameter('history_gate', None)
        if mode in ('static', 'adaptive'):
            self.gate_bias = nn.Parameter(
                conv.weight.new_zeros(historical_taps))
        else:
            self.register_parameter('gate_bias', None)

    def forward(self, h, sequence, force_unit_gates=False):
        if h.ndim != 3 or tuple(h.shape[:2]) != tuple(sequence.shape):
            raise ValueError('Expected h BxLxC and sequence BxL')
        if h.shape[-1] != self.conv.in_channels or h.shape[1] < 1:
            raise ValueError('Invalid channels or sequence width')
        valid = sequence.ne(0)
        x = h.masked_fill(~valid.unsqueeze(-1), 0)
        if self.mode == 'ones':
            padding = self.dilation * (self.kernel_size - 1)
            result = self.conv(
                F.pad(x.transpose(1, 2), (padding, 0))).transpose(1, 2)
            return result.masked_fill(~valid.unsqueeze(-1), 0)

        adaptive = self.mode == 'adaptive' and not force_unit_gates
        current = (F.layer_norm(x, (x.shape[-1],), eps=self.eps)
                   if adaptive else None)
        result = x.new_zeros(*x.shape[:2], self.conv.out_channels)
        for tap in range(self.kernel_size):
            # Cross-correlation: final kernel tap sees current position.
            lag = (self.kernel_size - 1 - tap) * self.dilation
            if lag == 0:
                contribution = x
            else:
                if lag >= x.shape[1]:
                    continue
                past = F.pad(x[:, :-lag, :], (0, 0, lag, 0))
                past_valid = F.pad(valid[:, :-lag], (lag, 0), value=False)
                if force_unit_gates:
                    contribution = past
                else:
                    logits = self.gate_bias[tap]
                    if adaptive:
                        normalized_past = F.layer_norm(
                            past, (past.shape[-1],), eps=self.eps)
                        logits = (
                            (current * self.current_gate[tap]).sum(-1)
                            + (normalized_past * self.history_gate[tap]).sum(-1)
                            + logits)
                    gate = 2.0 * torch.sigmoid(logits)
                    gate = gate * (valid & past_valid).to(x.dtype)
                    contribution = past * gate.unsqueeze(-1)
            result = result + F.linear(
                contribution, self.conv.weight[:, :, tap], bias=None)
        if self.conv.bias is not None:
            result = result + self.conv.bias
        return result.masked_fill(~valid.unsqueeze(-1), 0)

# Zero gate initialization consumes no extra random draws.
#
# Block integration:
# Replace explicit left-pad + Conv1d on BCL by adapter(h_BLC, sequence).
# Remove the old padding for that operation. Preserve original channel
# transposes, norms, activations, dropout, residuals and intermediate masks.
#
# Before fitting, compare force_unit_gates=True against an original causal
# convolution with identical Parameters and masks. Check outputs and gradients
# of h, weight and bias using the SAME random upstream tensor. Include K=1,
# short sequences, nonzero biases, multiple dilations and padding patterns.
# Declare numerical tolerances and report maximum errors; no bitwise claim.
# The force_unit_gates switch is a diagnostic intervention, never a second
# predictor or score-fusion path. Normal deployed calls leave it False.
#

originality.positive: Defines a precise, identity-initialized adaptation that modulates historical contributions within the existing causal NextItNet backbone.
originality.negative: Dynamic convolution, temporal gating and content-dependent filtering are established. The additive scalar gate provides limited pairwise expressivity, so the proposal warrants a modest adaptation claim.

future_potential.positive: Provides a controlled experimental handle on historical filtering and a path toward separately tested interaction gates without new data or independent predictors.
future_potential.negative: Residual paths preserve historical information, gates can learn item or frequency shortcuts, and neither current diagnostics nor the small prior validation difference establishes that temporal filtering is the main bottleneck.

code_difficulty.positive: Preserves original convolution Parameters, the scoring interface and the existing data pipeline; the core adapter is compact.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable implementation requires block-forward edits, gradient equivalence checks, runtime profiling, predictor synchronization, revised structural diagnostics and budgeted four-category controls.

related_work.title: NextItNet
contributions: Uses residual causal dilated convolutions for sequential recommendation.
Supplies the backbone preserved by the proposed tap-gating experiment.
limitations: Structural receptive-field coverage does not establish which historical interactions improve recommendations.
Does not establish gains for the proposed gates under the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: Pay Less Attention with Lightweight and Dynamic Convolutions
contributions: Compares static lightweight convolution with input-dependent dynamic convolution.
Provides a direct precedent for adaptive temporal filtering conditioned on the current representation.
limitations: Its machine-translation evidence does not establish sequential-recommendation gains.
Dynamic kernel prediction does not validate this particular current-plus-past scalar gate.

related_work.title: Sampled-softmax analysis (2024)
contributions: Analyzes the importance of temperature and negative sampling in recommendation training.
Motivates moderate multi-negative training as a separate objective hypothesis.
limitations: Does not establish improvement for this NextItNet benchmark.
Concentrated gradients and false negatives require care when increasing negative difficulty.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can yield model orderings inconsistent with full-catalog metrics.
Supports limiting claims to the prescribed sampled validation objective.
limitations: Does not invalidate the host's fixed comparison objective.
Does not provide full-catalog outcomes for these models.

related_work.title: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
contributions: Provides a paired bootstrap precedent for comparing systems on common observations.
Motivates resampling the same users for both recommenders within each category.
limitations: The category-stratified recommendation adaptation must be specified explicitly.
An ordinary paired bootstrap does not account for training variability or adaptive model selection.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains overfitting of model-selection criteria and resulting optimistic performance estimates.
Motivates recording every inspected configuration and checkpoint and limiting claims about selected winners.
limitations: Does not quantify selection optimism for this specific search.
Does not authorize changing the benchmark splits or evaluator.

related_work.title: GAT4Rec (2024)
contributions: Uses a GRU-derived signal to gate representations before Transformer processing.
Motivates content-dependent filtering as an adjacent design direction.
limitations: Its architecture differs from causal dilated NextItNet.
Its evidence does not validate historical-tap gating or explicit pairwise compatibility.

related_work.title: PyTorch Conv1d documentation
contributions: Defines Conv1d cross-correlation, dilation, weight layout and bias semantics.
Supports the oldest-to-current tap mapping used by the adapter.
limitations: Mathematical equivalence does not imply bitwise equivalence across GPU kernels.
Documentation alone cannot verify the integration into the unavailable baseline source.
